facts.what: Tiered cascade waterfall on Josephine Creek in Wooroonooran National Park (Bellenden Ker/Palmerston section), Far North Queensland; short walking track from a day-use car park with toilets, picnic tables and shelter; creek can flash-flood at any time of year; viewing platforms and swimming area have a temporary closure 2 Nov 2026 to 28 Feb 2027

facts.what: Concrete gravity dam on the Dee River near Mount Morgan, the town's main drinking-water source, also called the Big Dam; surrounds have playgrounds, barbecues, picnic areas, toilets; fishing for yellowbelly, saratoga and redclaw; camping prohibited

number-7-dam.cost_notes: No entry charge found; council parks page lists it as a public park with picnic facilities. Fishing needs a SIP permit (not the price).
number-7-dam.ticketUrl_note: Rockhampton Regional Council, managing agency; title 'No. 7 Dam Rockhampton Regional Council' (loaded OK).
unverified: no explicit 'free' statement on council page (page body not extracted)

facts.what: Oil and gas heritage attraction at 2 Riggers Road, Roma: Oil Patch Museum with vintage equipment and machinery, Peter Keegan Museum, Big Rig Tower and Tree Walk with views over Roma, Oil Patch Challenge for kids, evening Night Show; run by Maranoa Regional Council tourism; Self Guided Tour about 50 minutes

cost: https://bigrigroma.rezdy.com (operator's booking page: Self Guided Tour from AUD 20.00; Night Show from 20; Day and Night 35)

the-big-rig.cost_notes: Self Guided Tour adult from AUD 20 on the operator's own Rezdy store; Outback Queensland lists indicative rates $15 to $55 for the site's range of products.
the-big-rig.ticketUrl_note: Official site (tourism@maranoa.qld.gov.au; title 'The Big Rig - Experience a Slice of Roma's History'); bigrig.com.au is an unrelated wheel-accessories business, do not use.
the-big-rig.suggest_category: museum is fine (also a tower walk)
unverified: whether the AUD 20 is adult-only (page does not label it) and current 2026-27 price

facts.what: Rock-filled embankment dam on the Boyne River, South Burnett, built 1980-83, forming Lake Boondooma; lookout, picnic areas, boat ramp, toilets, BBQs, privately run camping and cabins; swimming, sailing, fishing (Stocked Impoundment Permit required)

boondooma-dam.cost_notes: Day visit to lookout and picnic areas: no fee found; camping is private and not the price; SIP fishing permit is an extra, not the price.
boondooma-dam.ticketUrl_note: Sunwater (owner) page, title 'Boondooma Dam – Sunwater'; facilities managed by South Burnett Regional Council.
unverified: no explicit statement that day use is free

facts.what: 161 km rail trail from Wulkuraka (Ipswich) via Somerset Region to Yarraman (Toowoomba Region) on the old Brisbane Valley railway line; open to walkers, touring cyclists and horse riders; longest rail trail in Queensland and Australia; gravel, off-road, traffic-free

brisbane-valley-rail-trail.cost_notes: No trail fee found on the user association site or Wikipedia; bike hire and shuttles are extras.
brisbane-valley-rail-trail.ticketUrl_note: BVRT Users Association site ('everything you need to know'; title names the trail). Not an agency; councils (Somerset, Ipswich, Toowoomba) manage it and no single council page was found (somerset.qld.gov.au/brisbane-valley-rail-trail 404). Orchestrator may prefer this or none.

facts.what: Open-air museum at Miles with about 30 buildings in a 1920s-style streetscape, plus war museum, lapidary and shell collections, Hippong Homestead, steam train and Great Artesian Basin display; ticket valid for the next day too; guided tours pre-booked (2 to 10 people)

cost: https://www.mhv.org.au/book-now (Entry adult $24; entry plus guided tour $34)

miles-historical-village.cost_notes: Adult entry $24.00 on operator's ticket page (seniors $21, students $12, under school age free).
miles-historical-village.ticketUrl_note: Operator site, title 'Miles Historical Village Museum' (loaded OK); deep link https://www.mhv.org.au/book-now also verified.

facts.what: Earth and rock-fill dam on Barker Creek near Wondai/Moffatdale, forming Lake Barambah; opened 1988; boat ramps, lookout, picnic areas, BBQs, toilets; swimming, kayaking, sailing; fishing needs a SIP permit; private camping; eastern facilities managed by South Burnett Regional Council, north-west by Sunwater

bjelke-petersen-dam.cost_notes: No day-use fee found; camping is private, fishing permit an extra.

facts.what: Heritage-listed pre-Federation fort on Green Hill, Thursday Island, built 1891-93 against a feared Russian threat; three six-inch breech-loading guns remain; reused as WWII signals and wireless station; underground bunker museum on pearling, shipping and military history; handed to Torres Shire Council as a public park and tourist attraction in 1993

cost: https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Thursday_Island (fort ruins free; bunker entry $4; bunker open to tour groups or pre-organised)

green-hill-fort.cost_notes: Fort ruins above ground free per Wikivoyage; $4 bunker museum is an extra inside it, not the price; no agency confirmation found.
green-hill-fort.ticketUrl_note: No official site found (TSIRC site loaded but has no fort page; ownership of fort unclear: Torres Strait Regional Authority/Historical Society sources conflict).
unverified: free access from an official source

facts.what: Split Rock Galleries, about 12 to 15 km south of Laura on Cape York: Quinkan rock art sites (paintings, engravings, hand stencils thought up to 14,000 years old) on sandstone escarpments, the only Quinkan site open to the public without a guide; 30-minute self-guided walk past three sites (Split Rock Galleries, Flying Fox Art Site, Tall Spirits Art Site); uneven rocky ground; guided tours booked via the Quinkan Cultural Centre (Ang-Gnarra Aboriginal Corporation)

cost: https://www.exploroz.com/places/122333/qld+split-rock ('cost for a self guided tour is now $40 per person'; third party)

split-rock.cost_notes: Self-guided fee $40 pp per ExploreOz; other listings $30 to $33; Wikipedia 'small fee'; operator page has no price, so treat as approximate.
split-rock.ticketUrl_note: Operator page headed 'Split Rock Art | Ang Gnarra Aborigina' (loaded OK).
split-rock.suggest_category: historic (or nature); placement has 'museum', which misdescribes an open-air rock art site
unverified: current self-guided fee ($30 to $40, sources conflict)
